This is not a coincidence. This is a confession.

 1913. The Federal Reserve Act was signed into law, creating a private central bank that controls the money supply of the United States. The same year, the 16th Amendment introduced the federal income tax — forcing every American to pay a percentage of their labor to the government.

Before 1913, there was no income tax. No central bank. No national debt. Americans kept 100% of what they earned.

Now look at what else happened between 1890 and 1913:

— The last references to “Tartary” disappeared from encyclopedias
— The Smithsonian collected and “lost” thousands of giant skeletons
— The orphan trains completed their final runs
— The last Kirkbride asylums were filled to capacity
— The World’s Fairs showcased their final “temporary” cities
— Free energy technology was suppressed (Tesla’s funding cut in 1904, Wardenclyffe demolished in 1917)

The old world operated without banks. Without debt. Without income tax. The energy was free. The architecture was inherited. The land belonged to no one because it belonged to everyone.

You cannot CONTROL a population that has free energy, free land, and no debt.

So you introduce scarcity. You meter the energy. You fence the land. You create “money” backed by nothing. You loan it at interest. You tax the labor. And suddenly, every human being on Earth is born into DEBT.

The Federal Reserve wasn’t created to “stabilize the economy.” It was created to ENSLAVE the survivors of the reset.

You do realize AI is already making decisions for you, right?

A lot of people still think, “I don't use AI. All that ChatGPT stuff is a whole different world that has nothing to do with me.”

But if you dig just a little deeper, you'll realize AI is already built into almost every part of our lives:

• Money. At many of the world's largest banks, AI evaluates loan applications. It looks at your spending patterns, transfers, and even how you use the banking app.

• Work. Algorithms rank millions of résumés and decide which candidates recruiters see first. You might get rejected without a single person ever reviewing your application — because the system never showed it to anyone.

• Shopping. Marketplaces don't necessarily show you the best products. They show you the ones you're most likely to buy.

And those are just a few examples. The crazy part is that all of this has happened in just the last few years, which means we're still only at the very beginning of the AI era.

The next step is AI agents that don't just give advice or analyze information — they actually take action. For example, they'll find the right product, wait for it to go on sale, and buy it for you.

Google has already started rolling out that kind of infrastructure.

So at the very least, we're headed toward a fascinating future — one where the very nature of the internet could fundamentally change.
